messages.subject: getting fit indices with sem.mi
parts:
Hello i am testing a mediation model with 40 imputed data sets with sem.mi function. when i use summary(fit,, fmi=TRUE,, standardize=TRUE, rsquare=TRUE, , ci=TRUE) i do not get fit indices of the model and if i add fit.indices=TRUE or fit.measures = ,c ("RMSEA", etc) it gives me the unused argument error. Does anybody know how i could fix this?







Thank you,
Mone Ionut

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: getting fit indices with sem.mi
parts:
you have to use the anova function for .mi objects. This will calculate the pooled fit indices, there are a couple of methods to pooled them, the object by default picks the best method depending on the estimator used in fit_mi

anova(fit_mi, indices=T)

Hey, this is my code!

library(semTools)
library(lavaan)
library(Amelia)
library(mice)
r2 <- r[,c("TraditionAndConformity", "Relatedness", "AgencyAndSelfDirectedness", "SelfDirectionActionC", "ConformityRulesC", "AutoRelEthno", "Heteroetno", "SeparatenessEtno", "IOSTOTAL", "dispototal")]
simpleMediation <- '
AutoRelEthno ~ b * Relatedness + c * IOSTOTAL
Relatedness ~ a * IOSTOTAL
indirect := a * b
total    := c + (a * b)
'
require(lavaan)
fit <- sem.mi(model = simpleMediation, data = r2, m = 40, miPackage = "Amelia", seed = 12345)
summary(fit, , standardize=TRUE, rsquare=TRUE, , ci=TRUE)
anova(fit,indices=T)
